basis: Plasma cell malignancy; destructive bone lesions occur in most patients. Renal insufficiency is less common than in secretory myeloma and does not clearly meet 30%.
Thymic epithelial tumor; thymus is outside the listed anatomical axes. Associated myasthenia and red cell aplasia are separate diseases; this is not lymphoma.
Carcinoma arising in the labia minora, a reproductive organ excluded from the axes; the generic skin carcinoma ancestry does not establish a separate cutaneous origin.
Ketogenesis defect; hepatic steatosis in 4/5 and elevated transaminases in 13/16; encephalopathy in 9/10 and seizures in 13/14 support common hepatic and brain dysfunction.
Respiratory ciliary dysfunction causes chronic rhinosinusitis and bronchiectasis (9/12). No subtype-specific evidence establishes common hearing damage; infections are secondary.
Ross River virus infection is defined clinically by inflammatory polyarthritis, often prolonged. Fever and transient rash do not establish additional organ damage.
Alpha-latrotoxin directly disrupts presynaptic neurotransmission. Muscle spasms and autonomic signs do not establish intrinsic muscle or cardiovascular damage.
VZV reactivation directly causes ganglionitis/neuritis and vesicular skin lesions. Ocular and otologic disease occur in minority subtypes.
Open spinal dysraphism involves vertebral defects and exposed spinal neural tissue. Bladder and bowel symptoms reflect neural injury; intrinsic urinary or intestinal damage is not established.
Defined by disease of erythrocytes. Infection and extrahematologic injury do not apply across this heterogeneous umbrella.
Eye, tooth and skeletal malformations define the syndrome; developmental delay occurs in 1/2. Sparse hair (1/2) omitted under the four-axis cap.
Teratoma arises within the central nervous system; mixed tumor tissue does not imply disease of other organs.
Isolated inherited prelingual sensorineural hearing loss.
Hepatic phosphorylase kinase deficiency causes liver glycogen storage; erythrocyte activity is normal.
FAR1 superactivity disrupts ether-lipid metabolism; spastic paraparesis and cataracts occur in 12/12. Constipation (5/12) alone does not establish direct intestinal damage.
Cerebral white matter disease with subcortical cysts, seizures and developmental impairment; all reported patients have neurologic involvement.
Cardiac defects and characteristic skeletal abnormalities define Noonan syndrome. Hemostatic dysfunction with bruising occurs in 57%; ptosis in 57%. Intellectual disability is below 30%.
Macular cone dystrophy causes central visual loss in 6/6. MFSD8 association alone does not establish a neurologic storage disorder in this phenotype.
Inherited combined glycosylation defects; neurodevelopmental impairment affects most multisystem forms. Hepatic, hematologic, immune and muscle involvement varies substantially by subtype.
Severe developmental impairment and cataracts occur in 6/6; kyphosis in 2/6 (~33%) supports skeletal involvement. Reported immunodeficiency lacks a qualifying frequency.
Cutis laxa and skeletal malformations define disease; learning disability in 3/7 (43%) and hearing impairment in 3/8 (38%). Proptosis alone does not establish ocular damage.
Defined by involvement of the parasympathetic nervous system; no additional organ damage is shared across the umbrella.
Inherited myopia is an ocular refractive and growth disorder.
Cerebellar hypoplasia and ataxia define disease; distal thumb phalanx abnormalities are frequent (30-79%). Nystagmus and oculomotor apraxia reflect neurologic dysfunction.
Acetylcholinesterase inhibition directly disrupts autonomic, central and neuromuscular transmission. Acute secretions and bronchospasm do not establish lasting pulmonary damage.
